Sloop, Nassau

Winslow Homer, 1899

Watercolour and graphite on paper

Sailing boat on a choppy sea, in loose watercolour washes of teal, grey and white.

Use this style

Winslow Homer, Sloop, Nassau, 1899. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Winslow Homer painted Sloop, Nassau during a winter trip to the Bahamas in 1898 and 1899. A small sailing boat leans in a fresh wind on a choppy turquoise sea under grey clouds. The Metropolitan Museum of Art bought it in 1910, the year Homer died.

Homer was one of the great American watercolourists. Here he works fast and wet: transparent washes for the sea and sky, the white of the paper left bare for the sails and the foam, and a few darker strokes for the hull and the waves.

How it looks on your photo

The model gives photos a soft, washed look in teal, grey and white, and dissolves fine detail into broad, watery areas. It suits seascapes, skies and calm landscapes. It is a gentle style, so try it at full intensity.
